speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, lower leg swelling, and weight loss. To better understand what's happening, have you noticed any changes in your urine output or the color of your urine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of chronic bronchitis and these new symptoms, have you noticed any foamy urine or changes in your urine color? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Serum_Creatinine, and Albumin.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein 4+, Blood Negative, Glucose Negative, WBC 0–1/hpf, Fatty Casts Numerous; Serum_Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL; Albumin: 1.8 mg/dL

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Lower leg swelling, Unintentional weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning, as pneumonia typically presents with cough and fever rather than significant edema and weight loss; have you noticed any shortness of breath or orthopnea (difficulty breathing when lying flat)? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

Also, has your urine become foamy or decreased in volume recently?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray: Right upper lobe density.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray shows a right upper lobe density, which could indicate a tumor rather than typical pneumonia given your significant weight loss and edema. Has your urine appeared foamy, or have you noticed any recent swelling in your hands or face? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Serum_AFP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein 4+, Blood Negative, Glucose Negative, WBC 0–1/hpf, Fatty Casts Numerous; Serum_AFP: Not Provided

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome (specifically, likely nephrotic syndrome secondary to malignancy or metastasis).
